title: Prefix Executability: Evaluating Tool-Using Agents Beyond Final Success
abstract: arXiv:2610.40444v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Tool-use benchmarks often score agents by final task success, but terminal outcomes can obscure whether the intermediate tool-call trajectory was executable. We propose prefix executability as a trajectory-level evaluation protocol for tool-using agents. The protocol measures whether every prefix of a predicted tool-call sequence remains executable under tool schemas, state preconditions, and data dependencies, and summarizes reliability using Prefix Executability Curves (PEC), First-Error Depth (FED), Trajectory Executability Rate (TER), horizon-normalized AUC-PEC, and Recovery Rate (RR). We instantiate the protocol on stratified samples from BFCL-v3 multi-turn and ToolSandbox, and on the complete Airline/Retail base splits of $\tau^3$-bench. We observe that outcome-only and prefix-level rankings diverge: agents whose execution is conditioned on an unverified plan often achieve higher point-estimate final success than non-plan-condition

translated_title: 前缀可执行性：超越最终成功率的工具使用智能体评估
translated_abstract: 工具使用基准测试通常以最终任务是否成功来为智能体评分，但终端结果可能掩盖中间工具调用轨迹是否可执行。我们提出前缀可执行性作为一种面向工具使用智能体的轨迹级评估协议。该协议衡量预测的工具调用序列的每一个前缀在工具模式、状态前置条件和数据依赖约束下是否保持可执行，并通过前缀可执行性曲线（PEC）、首次错误深度（FED）、轨迹可执行率（TER）、视界归一化 AUC-PEC 以及恢复率（RR）来总结智能体的可靠性。我们在 BFCL-v3 多轮对话和 ToolSandbox 的分层样本上，以及在 τ³-bench 完整的 Airline/Retail 基础数据集划分上实例化了该协议。我们观察到仅基于最终结果的排名与前缀级别的排名存在分歧：其执行以未经核实的计划为条件的智能体，其点估计最终成功率往往高于非计划条件（的智能体）……
tldr: 该论文提出“前缀可执行性”这一轨迹级评估协议，通过检验工具调用序列每个前缀的可执行性并引入PEC、FED、TER等新指标，揭示出仅凭最终任务成功率评估智能体会掩盖其中间执行轨迹的可靠性差异。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes "prefix executability," a trajectory-level evaluation protocol that checks whether every prefix of an agent's tool-call sequence remains executable using new metrics such as PEC, FED, and TER, revealing that final-success-only rankings diverge from prefix-level reliability rankings.
